title: Control of Purple Nutsedge in Maize

Header: Control of Purple Nutsedge in Maize

Prevention: Tubers are the main means of spread, clean tools and farm machinery to prevent introduction to new fields
Use of cover and/or intercropping with legumes, such as cowpea, beans, dolichos species, to prevent weed establishment
Use of deep tillage (>12cm) to expose tubers and rhizomes to direct sunlight.
Tubers can be destroyed by dessication (most effective in dry soil)
Control established populations near waterways to prevent spread during flooding and storm events
Monitoring: Erect, perennial sedge (30-60 cm high), with extensive underground network of tubers.
Tubers dark brown/black, irregular shaped, 1-2 cm long at maturity, with several buds.
Leaves linear with distinct midrib, 7 mm wide.
Inflorescence with several unequal 'branches', each 2-6 cm long, emerging from the tip of the stem; each with 3-8 purplish- brown flowerheads.
Inspect fields fortnightly, in particular during and shortly after the wet season, and consider direct control when found
Look out for it in wetlands and along waterways.
Water and storm events can spread tubers
Direct Control: Hand-weeding at least 2 times until crop canopy formed: the weed is shade intolerant
Restrictions: Use of chemical herbicides may lead to the development of herbicide resistance.
When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label, such as dosage
Halosulfuron methyl to control the weeds according to the manufacturer's instructions
Glyhposate, applied on actively growing weeds according to the manufacturer's instructions
